questions.stem: Humans have a double circulatory system, meaning blood passes through the heart twice per complete circuit. What is the advantage of this compared to a single circulatory system (as in fish)?

options.text: It uses less energy than a single circulatory system
Blood pressure is boosted after passing through the lungs, allowing faster delivery of oxygenated blood to the body tissues
It allows blood to carry more carbon dioxide
Blood only needs to flow in one direction

questions.explanation: In a single circulatory system (fish), blood loses pressure as it passes through the gill capillaries, so it flows slowly through the body. In a double system, blood returns to the heart from the lungs and is pumped again at high pressure to the body. This means oxygenated blood reaches the tissues more quickly and efficiently, supporting the higher metabolic rate of mammals.

questions.stem: The pulmonary circuit carries blood between the heart and lungs. Unusually, the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood. Why is it still called an artery?

options.text: Because it contains valves
Because arteries are defined as vessels that carry blood AWAY from the heart, regardless of oxygenation
Because it was named incorrectly in the past
Because it carries blood at low pressure

questions.explanation: Arteries are defined by their direction of blood flow (away from the heart), not by whether the blood is oxygenated. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. Similarly, the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood back to the heart. This is a common exam misconception.

questions.stem: A doctor measures a patient's heart rate at 72 beats per minute and their stroke volume at 70 ml. What is their cardiac output?

options.text: 142 ml per minute
5040 ml per minute (approximately 5 litres)
1.03 ml per beat
7200 ml per minute

questions.explanation: Cardiac output = heart rate x stroke volume = 72 x 70 = 5040 ml per minute (about 5 litres). This means the heart pumps approximately 5 litres of blood per minute at rest -- roughly the entire blood volume. During exercise, cardiac output increases significantly.

questions.stem: An insect has an open circulatory system where blood (haemolymph) bathes the organs directly. Why would this system be inadequate for a large, active mammal?

options.text: Insect blood is a different colour
An open system has low blood pressure and slow flow, which cannot deliver oxygen and nutrients fast enough for a mammal's high metabolic rate
Mammals have too few organs for an open system
Open systems only work in cold environments

questions.explanation: Mammals have high metabolic rates and need rapid, efficient delivery of oxygen and nutrients and removal of waste. A closed circulatory system (blood confined to vessels) maintains high pressure and directed flow, enabling fast transport. An open system has low pressure and slow, undirected flow, which is adequate for small insects but not large mammals.

questions.stem: Blood from the digestive system travels to the liver via the hepatic portal vein before entering the general circulation. Why is this routing important?

options.text: The liver adds oxygen to the blood
The liver processes absorbed nutrients (e.g., regulates glucose levels, detoxifies harmful substances) before they reach the rest of the body
The liver stores all the blood from digestion
Blood must be filtered to remove food particles

questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood from the intestines to the liver, which acts as a processing centre. The liver regulates blood glucose levels (storing excess as glycogen), detoxifies alcohol and drugs, processes amino acids (deamination), and removes harmful substances before the blood enters the general circulation.
